what_happened: The person running Athena deleted by hand the 16 GB writer build folder of job 20261027-054228-k9ex, the verifier-timeout job. The job was held on low disk, not failed. No acceptance criterion, check or finding failed. This was the third job held today by the disk-check ordering, where the free-space check runs before the job's own regenerable build is removed. The fix for that ordering is itself held, and so are its dependents. Their hold records are passed over by later batches instead of being resumed, so the person running Athena broke the loop by hand.
cause: Athena's disk guard and its build-freeing step were built as separate changes with no fixed order and no check that they agree. The guard counts a regenerable build as space the job still needs. The hold only waits and frees nothing. The repair is an ordinary queued job that needs the same disk, so the fault blocks its own fix. Nothing prioritizes the repair or exempts it from the guard. Held jobs are also not resumed automatically once space returns, because later batches skip their hold records. Hand cleanups therefore repeat, and this is at least the tenth.
prevention: Tie the disk lifecycle to build state in code. Before the free-space check, and whenever a job is held on low disk, automatically remove the job's own finished or orphaned regenerable writer build, then re-measure free space. Only hold if space is still short after that. Make drain resume held jobs, including their hold records, once space is available. Run the disk-ordering fix first and let it bypass the guard it repairs.
proposed_request: Fix the low-disk hold so that a job is never held because of its own regenerable build. Outcome: when the free-disk guard would hold a job, Athena first deletes that job's own finished or orphaned writer build, and any build of an interrupted job, then re-measures free space. It holds the job only if space is still below the limit. Drain must also pick up held jobs whose hold records exist and resume them once free space meets the limit, instead of passing over them. Acceptance: (1) a test with a job whose own 16 GB-style build is the only thing keeping free space under the limit shows the job proceeds to checks without any hand deletion; (2) a test shows a held job with a hold record is resumed by the next drain once space allows; (3) a test shows a job is still held when space is short after its own build is removed. Priority: urgent. This job must run ahead of the other held jobs and its disk need must not be blocked by the guard it fixes. Dependent jobs, including the verifier-timeout job 20261027-054228-k9ex, should resume afterward.
